news.headline: Govt proposes major CSR rule changes, seeks to include mental health, clean energy, PM internship scheme
news.story_lead: Govt proposes major CSR rule changes, seeks to include mental health, clean energy, PM internship scheme Govt proposes new CSR rules: adds mental health, clean energy & internships, while banning one-off events & product freebies, plus stricter NGO oversight. The government has proposed amendments to corporate social responsibility norms, including allowing initiatives in mental health, career counselling, the PM Internship Scheme and clean energy as eligible activities under the companies law. Besides, one-off events, financing of government schemes, corpus fund contributions and in-kind contributions of a company's own products, other than immediate disaster relief, are proposed to be excluded from the CSR ambit.
news.full_article_text: Govt proposes major CSR rule changes, seeks to include mental health, clean energy, PM internship scheme Govt proposes new CSR rules: adds mental health, clean energy & internships, while banning one-off events & product freebies, plus stricter NGO oversight. The government has proposed amendments to corporate social responsibility norms, including allowing initiatives in mental health, career counselling, the PM Internship Scheme and clean energy as eligible activities under the companies law. Besides, one-off events, financing of government schemes, corpus fund contributions and in-kind contributions of a company's own products, other than immediate disaster relief, are proposed to be excluded from the CSR ambit. A certain class of profitable companies are required to shell out at least two per cent of their three-year average annual profit towards Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities in a financial year. The corporate affairs ministry has proposed amendments to the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, as well as Schedule VII, which provides a broad list of areas where activities can be eligible under the CSR framework. To expand the scope of CSR activities, the ministry has mooted inclusion of mental health, telemedicine, career counselling, the PM Internship Scheme, clean energy and waste management, including e-waste management, under Schedule VII. Also, animal welfare, marine conservation and sports infrastructure are to be included. Also read: Who is holding the soul of your organisation? The ministry's proposed amendments also seek to put in place a stronger oversight mechanism for implementing agencies wherein the registration of an agency can be cancelled, and once done, there will be a three-year ban on re-registration for the particular agency. Among other amendments, the ministry has proposed that international organisations headquartered in India can be eligible for functioning as CSR implementing agencies. As per the proposed changes, all CSR-mandated companies may commission independent impact assessments. Also read: Fadnavis flags malnutrition in Mumbai slums, calls for targeted CSR interventions Amit Agarwal, Senior Partner at advisory firm Nangia & Co LLP, said the proposed amendments aim to marry the actual spend with the objectives of the CSR framework. "CSR will increasingly be judged not by how much is spent, but by what it achieves on the ground. "... distributing one's own products free of cost has often worked more as brand promotion than as social responsibility. The exclusions draw a clear line between genuine impact and freebies, events or idle corpus funds," he said. In a public notice, the ministry said it has reviewed the existing CSR ecosystem. "... to further strengthen business involvement in CSR, suggestions were invited from various stakeholders, so that the ministry could facilitate businesses to be even more socially, economically, and environmentally responsible. "Multiple suggestions were received from various stakeholders to propose various changes in the CSR framework," it said. Also read: Why disability needs to move beyond CSR The ministry has sought stakeholders' comments on the proposed amendments to the rules till December 11. Anjali Malhotra, Partner - Regulatory at consultancy Nangia Global, said the proposed measures are expected to strengthen regulatory oversight, promote greater transparency and accountability in the allocation and utilisation of CSR funds.

news.headline: Man accused in Andhra chainsaw attack discharged from hospital, girl shows signs of recovery
news.story_lead: Man accused in Andhra chainsaw attack discharged from hospital, girl shows signs of recovery The 21-year-old accused in the chainsaw attack on a Class 10 girl in Andhra Pradesh was discharged from hospital and taken back to jail after his health improved. The 21-year-old man accused of attacking a Class 10 student with a chainsaw at Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu, Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district, was discharged from the Kurnool Government General Hospital, police said on Thursday. Doctors said on Wednesday that Hemanth alias Dummu, who was shot at by police while allegedly attempting to escape custody, was discharged following improvement in his health condition.
news.full_article_text: Man accused in Andhra chainsaw attack discharged from hospital, girl shows signs of recovery The 21-year-old accused in the chainsaw attack on a Class 10 girl in Andhra Pradesh was discharged from hospital and taken back to jail after his health improved. The 21-year-old man accused of attacking a Class 10 student with a chainsaw at Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu, Andhra Pradesh’s Anantapur district, was discharged from the Kurnool Government General Hospital, police said on Thursday. Doctors said on Wednesday that Hemanth alias Dummu, who was shot at by police while allegedly attempting to escape custody, was discharged following improvement in his health condition. “He responded well to treatment and his health parameters were now normal. His blood pressure, pulse rate and electrocardiogram (ECG) reports were all within normal limits, indicating that he had recovered sufficiently,” Kurnool hospital superintendent Dr K Venkateshwarlu said. The doctors submitted their medical report to the judge of the local court in the afternoon, following which the police took Hemanth back to Anantapur, where he was lodged in Reddipalli jail, a police officer said. Hemanth had allegedly entered the school premises carrying a chainsaw and attacked the student on October 31. Doctors at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru informed the state government that the girl, who suffered serious injuries, was showing significant signs of recovery. State minister for education and information technology Nara Lokesh said in a statement that he had held a video conference with the medical team at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru in the morning to review the health condition of the 15-year-old girl. “Her major wounds had healed and the stitches had been removed, while treatment for a few minor injuries was continuing... Her confidence was gradually returning, they added, describing her as a fighter who had displayed extraordinary courage during her battle for survival,” he said. Hours after he was caught in the Atmakur forests on November 1, Hemanth was being taken to Rapthadu for a reconstruction of the crime scene when he allegedly tried to flee and hurled stones at the police personnel escorting him. “When the police were bringing him to Raptadu to reconstruct the scene of the offence he had committed at the school, he tried to escape and started hurling stones at the police personnel. Several police personnel sustained injuries in the attack, when they tried to overpower him,” an officer said. Hemanth was initially admitted to the Anantapur government hospital for treatment, where his right leg was amputated. The Anantapur police shifted Hemanth on November 13 following the deterioration of his health condition. The medical team at the Anantapur hospital submitted a status report to the high court stating that the blood clots in his blood vessels could pose a serious threat to his life if not treated immediately. The clots could travel to vital organs, including the heart, brain and lungs, potentially resulting in fatal complications. The medical team said that the Anantapur hospital lacked the necessary infrastructure, including a heart-lung machine and other specialised facilities required to remove the clots. After obtaining permission from the court, the police shifted him to Kurnool Government General Hospital in an Armed Reserve (AR) escort vehicle, accompanied by around 10 police personnel. Kurnool hospital superintendent Dr Venkateshwarlu said, “We provided all necessary medical treatment in accordance with the court’s directions and that the accused was declared medically fit for discharge.” - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Srinivasa Rao Apparasu Srinivasa Rao is Senior Assistant Editor based out of Hyderabad covering developments in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana . He has over three decades of reporting experience.

news.headline: Scientists flooded GTA’s Los Santos to simulate rising seas
news.story_lead: Scientists flooded GTA’s Los Santos to simulate rising seas They used a fan-built 3D model of the map, and pinned it to coordinates with 11 control points and set the sea level from 31 shoreline points The water reached Vespucci’s canals first. Then the Port of South Los Santos stopped working, followed by the gasworks and the sewage plant. Nobody in a stolen car caused any of this.
news.full_article_text: Scientists flooded GTA’s Los Santos to simulate rising seas They used a fan-built 3D model of the map, and pinned it to coordinates with 11 control points and set the sea level from 31 shoreline points The water reached Vespucci’s canals first. Then the Port of South Los Santos stopped working, followed by the gasworks and the sewage plant. Nobody in a stolen car caused any of this. The sea simply came in. That’s Los Santos, the sunbathed in-game version of Los Angeles of Grand Theft Auto V, in the face of a rising seas scenario modelled by Paul Nörenberg and Hugues Lantuit of the University of Potsdam and the Alfred Wegener Institute. Their paper coincides with the launch of the GTA VI video game. Los Santos, they say, serves as an ideal case study because it faithfully replicates the real Los Angeles, thereby enabling a direct comparison of simulated flood outcomes. The scientists are working with two Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) scenarios from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Fifth Assessment Report (AR5). The researchers used these scenarios to simulate the consequences of any future sea-level rise and demonstrate the exact ways the city in GTA V would change. The research notes that under the RCP 8.5 scenario with storm surges, combined sea levels are projected to reach 5.18 m by 2300, with the model showing 5.1 % of the mapped land area inundated; for a 2500 scenario with projected sea levels of 8.22 mm, this increases to 6.5 % modelled inundation, which places the port, wastewater infrastructure, and coastal energy facilities at risk. Under the RCP 2.6 mitigation scenario, the model shows 2.2 % of land area inundated at 2300 with storm surge, with no major infrastructure affected. “Many games have now advanced graphically to such an extent that they can reproduce real-world locations almost true to life,” says Paul Nörenberg, lead author of the study. Grand Theft Auto V (GTA V) is one of those games: it takes players to the fictional city of Los Santos. “The city is a near-exact replica of the real-life Los Angeles, with all its famous landmarks, neighbourhoods as well as urban and coastal features.” In 2017, four scientific modelling teams, from the Netherlands, US, Japan and Austria, coordinated through the Integrated Assessment Modeling Consortium (IAMC) to create four scenarios, which the United Nations’ IPCC published. Rockstar doesn’t release any raw terrain data. The scientists used a fan-built 3D model of the map, pinned it to coordinates with 11 control points and set the sea level from 31 shoreline points. This was checked by flying an in-game helicopter along the coastline. The height was calibrated against the game’s Mount Chiliad. They then simulated the IPCC scenarios for the years 2100, 2300 and 2500—each topped with a 1.59-metre storm surge, the highest Los Angeles has ever recorded. When the scientists overlaid the simulation data over real maps and flood studies for Los Angeles, the same districts in reality also stood most exposed. Vespucci floods like Venice Beach might, Chumash like Malibu, and the Port of South Los Santos is as vulnerable as the Port of LA. Rockstar Games, the developer, copied the city closely enough to inadvertently replicate its weak spots. Rockstar Games says GTA V is the second best-selling video game of all time, with more than 225 million copies sold in the last decade. There is a large community of players familiar with Los Santos. “If this familiar, personally explored virtual landscape changes, players can engage with the effects of climate change on an emotional level,” notes Nörenberg. “This can bridge a gap in a way that conventional visualisations, such as models or maps, struggle to achieve.” The scientists agree this isn’t without caveats. “We recommend the approach as a template for geoscience communication using open-world video game environments, with the explicit caveat that the static inundation model and its limitations must be communicated transparently to every audience, and that the 2300 and 2500 horizons remain the weakest part of the scenario set,” they say. A commercial video game is built for storytelling and action, not exactly for rigorous scientific modelling. news.full_article_text: Maharashtra puts non-essential construction on hold in 304 drought-hit talukas, prioritises relief The Maharashtra government has directed district authorities to temporarily suspend non-essential new construction works in 304 drought -hit talukas and divert available funds for drinking water supply and other drought-mitigation measures. A Government Resolution issued by the Planning Department on Wednesday said funds under the District Annual Plan (General) must be prioritised to finish incomplete water supply projects, strengthen existing water sources and ensure water and fodder availability for livestock. Also Read | Maharashtra adds 2 more talukas to drought-hit list; count rises to 310 The state has identified 304 talukas as drought-affected, and the government said immediate measures were necessary to meet the drinking water requirements of citizens, livestock and other essential needs. District collectors have been directed to review non-essential new projects, including parks, beautification works, new office and administrative buildings, cement roads, drains and other works involving substantial water consumption, and take steps to temporarily defer them in accordance with prescribed procedures. Funds available for such deferred projects will be reviewed and reallocated to priority drought-relief works in the affected talukas, the GR said, adding that the exercise of reallocation must be completed by December 31. The government has clarified that ongoing projects should not be stopped indiscriminately. Authorities must take decisions on a case-by-case basis after considering contractual obligations, public safety, the stage of work, expenditure already incurred and possible compensation or financial liabilities, it said. Essential works directly related to drinking water availability, strengthening existing water sources, creating necessary new sources, providing water and fodder for livestock, water conservation, irrigation, public health and emergency requirements have been exempted from the temporary suspension, subject to applicable rules and approvals. The GR also gives priority to completing incomplete pipelines, pumps, electricity connections, storage tanks and distribution systems required to transport water from existing sources to scarcity-hit villages. "Projects that can be completed during the current scarcity period and provide immediate access to water must receive priority. New projects that cannot normally be completed within the current financial year should not be sanctioned under the special priority framework," it said. In exceptional cases, essential drinking water, livestock water or water-source creation projects may be considered even if they extend beyond the current financial year. However, the additional financial liability for 2027-28 must not exceed 10 per cent of the approved District Annual Plan outlay for 2026-27. District collectors have been asked to convene meetings of district-level officials within seven days of the issuance of the GR and prepare an integrated taluka-wise and project-wise action plan within 15 days. The government has also provided for expedited approval of urgent drought-relief measures. If convening a District Planning Committee meeting would delay an essential intervention, the collector can submit a proposal to the guardian minister, who heads the committee, for approval, subject to ratification at its subsequent meeting. Collectors will have to review the progress of approved works and submit reports on fund allocation, expenditure and physical progress to the Planning and Finance departments by the 10th of every month. The GR also mandates the publication of details of sanctioned works, funds, expenditure and progress on district collectorate websites or government portals. The provisions will apply to the 304 drought-hit talukas and any additional talukas subsequently declared drought-affected or facing scarcity. The order will remain applicable for the 2026-27 financial year.

He also referred to objections he had raised over the manner in which the inquiry was conducted, saying he was reserving his right to challenge the findings. news.headline: Political Debate Erupts in Tamil Nadu Over Major Heroin Seizures and Narcotics Enforcement
news.story_lead: A major political row erupted in Tamil Nadu following large-scale drug interdictions by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence. Opposition figures raised concerns over law enforcement efficacy, while state police deployed creative digital campaigns against drug abuse coinciding with the global release of GTA VI.
news.full_article_text:
### Major Narcotics Interdictions in Tamil Nadu

Central law enforcement agencies executed significant drug busts in Tamil Nadu, sparking widespread political debate regarding state narcotics control. The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) intercepted a vehicle in Madhavaram, Chennai, confiscating 70 kg of heroin valued at ₹140 crore and arresting two individuals. This operation follows a prior DRI raid in Nagapattinam that seized contraband worth ₹270 crore linked to illicit distribution networks.

### Political Allegations and Public Debates

Following the seizures, DMK Chief M.K. Stalin criticized the TVK-led state administration under Chief Minister Vijay, characterizing the state's security situation as severely deteriorated. Drawing parallels to 'Vice City' from the Grand Theft Auto video game franchise, Stalin highlighted issues including rising illicit substance trafficking, alleged criminal misconduct, major robberies, and custodial deaths. He questioned why primary drug seizures were being conducted by federal agencies rather than the 65 state-level special task force teams dedicated to anti-narcotics operations.

AMMK General Secretary T.T.V. Dhinakaran also urged the state government to move beyond public awareness campaigns and execute concrete actions against drug networks distributing synthetic and organic narcotics across the state.

### Police Campaign and National Context

In response to public discourse, Tamil Nadu Police released anti-drug informational graphics themed after GTA VI artwork. Titled 'Grand Theft Demolisher' and 'Drive Against Drugs', the communications underscored police actions including digital map tracking of trafficking routes, suspect detentions, and student outreach campaigns.

Concurrently, Prime Minister Narendra Modi utilized the backdrop of the global release of GTA VI—coming 13 years after GTA V in 2013—to highlight India's national development metrics between 2013 and 2026. hindi_translation.story_lead: राजस्व खुफिया निदेशालय द्वारा मादक पदार्थों की बड़ी जब्ती के बाद तमिलनाडु में राजनीतिक बहस छिड़ गई। विपक्षी नेताओं ने कानून व्यवस्था पर सवाल उठाए, जबकि पुलिस ने जागरूकता अभियान जारी किया।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### तमिलनाडु में मादक पदार्थों की जब्ती और कार्रवाई

केन्द्रीय प्रवर्तन एजेंसियों ने तमिलनाडु में नशीली दवाओं की बड़ी खेप जब्त की, जिससे राज्य में कानून प्रवर्तन पर राजनीतिक चर्चा शुरू हो गई। राजस्व खुफिया निदेशालय (DRI) ने चेन्नई के माधवराम में एक वाहन को रोककर 140 करोड़ रुपये मूल्य की 70 किलोग्राम हेरोइन जब्त की और दो लोगों को गिरफ्तार किया। इससे पहले डीआरआई ने नागपट्टिनम में 270 करोड़ रुपये मूल्य के नशीले पदार्थ जब्त किए थे।

### राजनीतिक आरोप और प्रतिक्रियाएं

डीएमके प्रमुख एम.के. स्टालिन ने टीवीके नेतृत्व वाली राज्य सरकार की आलोचना करते हुए राज्य की कानून-व्यवस्था की स्थिति पर सवाल उठाए। उन्होंने मादक पदार्थों की तस्करी, आपराधिक घटनाओं और हिरासत में मौतों का जिक्र किया। उन्होंने पूछा कि राज्य की 65 विशेष टास्क फोर्स टीमों के बजाय केंद्रीय एजेंसियां ​​ही प्रमुख जब्तियां क्यों कर रही हैं।

वहीं एएमएमके महासचिव टी.टी.वी. दिनकरन ने भी सरकार से केवल जागरूकता अभियानों तक सीमित न रहकर नशीली दवाओं के नेटवर्क के खिलाफ सख्त प्रवर्तन कार्रवाई करने का आग्रह किया।

### जागरूकता अभियान और राष्ट्रीय संदर्भ

तमिलनाडु पुलिस ने डिजिटल पोस्टरों के माध्यम से नशीली दवाओं के खिलाफ जागरूकता अभियान चलाया। इन पोस्टरों में मैपिंग के जरिए तस्करी नेटवर्क को ट्रैक करने, गिरफ्तारियों और छात्रों के लिए जागरूकता सत्रों की जानकारी दी गई।

दूसरी ओर, प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने 2013 से 2026 के बीच भारत के विकास के संकेतकों की तुलना करते हुए एक 10-स्लाइड प्रस्तुति साझा की, जिसमें अर्थव्यवस्था, स्वच्छता, सौर ऊर्जा, रक्षा निर्यात और वामपंथी उग्रवाद में कमी जैसी उपलब्धियों को रेखांकित किया गया।

news.full_article_text:
### CBSE Three-Language Policy & Supreme Court Proceedings

The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has moved an application before the Supreme Court seeking to recall its interim order dated September 28, which had extended exemption from the mandatory three-language policy to Class VI students for the current academic session. Appearing before a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Aishwarya Bhati stated that minor administrative issues required resolution, following which the apex court scheduled the application for hearing in the upcoming week.

According to official enrolment metrics submitted by CBSE, out of more than 2.344 million students enrolled in Class VI across affiliated schools, approximately 99.82% (over 2.340 million) are already studying two native Indian languages. The Board emphasized that the court's relief effectively applies to only 4,186 students nationwide (roughly 0.18%) who are studying two foreign languages across 99 specific institutions.

### Infrastructure and Faculty Availability Data

To counter claims regarding lack of infrastructure, CBSE submitted national school statistics showing that India has 1,466,682 operational schools (CBSE and non-CBSE) catering to 247.21 million students. Of these, 33,017 schools are affiliated with CBSE, enrolling over 27.5 million students from Class I to XII. Within the 99 CBSE schools where 4,186 students pursue two foreign languages, 19,892 students in the same schools are studying two native languages, proving that facilities for teaching native languages are present.

CBSE informed the court that digital textbooks for Class VI across all 22 scheduled Indian languages listed in the Eighth Schedule are published on the NCERT portal, while SCERT resources cover remaining regional choices. On teacher deployment, out of 20,777 CBSE schools evaluated, approximately 93% possess instructors for at least two distinct indigenous languages, and 3,523 schools employ teachers for three or more native languages. The Centre had also created a five-member monitoring panel on September 16, headed by Education Ministry Director Bhagwati Prasad Kalal, alongside members from NCERT, CBSE, KVS, and NVS to oversee implementation.
news.background_context: On September 28, the Supreme Court granted Class VI students exemption from the three-language framework to align them with relief previously extended to Classes VII, VIII, and IX. Parents and students had filed petitions citing mid-year implementation uncertainty, lack of textbooks, and unready teaching infrastructure. CBSE challenged this, stating that affiliated schools have taught two native languages for decades and that mid-session exemptions disrupt established school timetables.

hindi_translation.story_lead: केन्द्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड (CBSE) ने उच्चतम न्यायालय का रुख कर 28 सितंबर के उस आदेश को वापस लेने की मांग की है, जिसके तहत कक्षा 6 के छात्रों को अनिवार्य त्रि-भाषा नीति से छूट दी गई थी। बोर्ड ने कहा कि इस छूट का लाभ देश भर में कक्षा 6 के 0.2% से भी कम छात्रों को मिलता है और इससे शैक्षणिक व्यवस्था प्रभावित होती है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### CBSE त्रि-भाषा नीति और सुप्रीम कोर्ट की कार्यवाही

केन्द्रीय माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड (CBSE) ने सुप्रीम कोर्ट में एक आवेदन दायर कर 28 सितंबर के अपने अंतरिम आदेश को वापस लेने का अनुरोध किया है, जिसने चालू शैक्षणिक वर्ष के लिए कक्षा 6 के छात्रों को अनिवार्य त्रि-भाषा नीति से छूट प्रदान की थी। भारत के मुख्य न्यायाधीश सूर्य कांत की अध्यक्षता वाली पीठ के समक्ष पेश होते हुए अतिरिक्त सॉलिसिटर जनरल (ASG) ऐश्वर्या भाटी ने कहा कि कुछ प्रशासनिक मुद्दों को सुलझाना आवश्यक है, जिसके बाद अदालत ने आवेदन पर अगले सप्ताह सुनवाई करने पर सहमति व्यक्त की।

बोर्ड द्वारा प्रस्तुत आधिकारिक आंकड़ों के अनुसार, सीबीएसई से संबद्ध स्कूलों में कक्षा 6 में नामांकित 2.344 मिलियन से अधिक छात्रों में से लगभग 99.82% (2.340 मिलियन से अधिक) छात्र पहले से ही दो देशी भारतीय भाषाओं का अध्ययन कर रहे हैं। बोर्ड ने स्पष्ट किया कि अदालत के आदेश का लाभ देश भर में केवल 4,186 छात्रों (लगभग 0.18%) को मिलता है, जो 99 स्कूलों में दो विदेशी भाषाओं की पढ़ाई कर रहे हैं।

### बुनियादी ढांचा और शिक्षकों की उपलब्धता के आंकड़े

संसाधनों की कमी के दावों का खंडन करते हुए CBSE ने राष्ट्रीय आंकड़े पेश किए, जिनके अनुसार भारत में कुल 1,466,682 स्कूल (सीबीएसई और गैर-सीबीएसई) हैं, जिनमें 247.21 मिलियन छात्र पंजीकृत हैं। इनमें से 33,017 स्कूल सीबीएसई से संबद्ध हैं, जिनमें कक्षा 1 से 12 तक 27.5 मिलियन से अधिक छात्र पढ़ते हैं। कक्षा 6 में दो विदेशी भाषाएं पढ़ा रहे 99 स्कूलों में भी 19,892 छात्र दो देशी भाषाओं का अध्ययन कर रहे हैं, जो दर्शाता है कि देशी भाषाओं के शिक्षण की व्यवस्था उपलब्ध है।

बोर्ड ने कोर्ट को बताया कि 8वीं अनुसूची की सभी 22 अनुसूचित भारतीय भाषाओं के लिए कक्षा 6 की डिजिटल पाठ्यपुस्तकें NCERT की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध हैं। इसके अलावा, 20,777 सीबीएसई स्कूलों के सर्वेक्षण में लगभग 93% स्कूलों के पास कम से कम दो देशी भाषाओं के शिक्षक उपलब्ध हैं और 3,523 स्कूलों में तीन या अधिक देशी भाषाओं के शिक्षक तैनात हैं। केंद्र सरकार ने 16 सितंबर को शिक्षा मंत्रालय के निदेशक भगवती प्रसाद कलाल की अध्यक्षता में 5 सदस्यीय समिति का भी गठन किया था।
hindi_translation.background_context: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 28 सितंबर को कक्षा 6 के छात्रों को त्रि-भाषा नीति से छूट दी थी ताकि उन्हें कक्षा 7, 8 और 9 के छात्रों के समान राहत मिल सके। छात्रों और अभिभावकों ने सत्र के मध्य में नीति लागू करने, पुस्तकों और शिक्षकों की कमी का हवाला देते हुए याचिकाएं दायर की थीं। CBSE ने इसका विरोध करते हुए कहा कि स्कूल दशकों से दो देशी भाषाएं पढ़ा रहे हैं और सत्र के बीच में छूट से शैक्षणिक व्यवस्था में अनिश्चितता पैदा होती है।
bullet_points: CBSE ने कक्षा 6 के छात्रों को त्रि-भाषा नीति से मिली छूट को वापस लेने के लिए सुप्रीम कोर्ट में याचिका दायर की।
आंकड़ों के अनुसार, 99.82% (23.4 लाख से अधिक) छात्र पहले से ही दो देशी भारतीय भाषाएं पढ़ रहे हैं।
छूट का प्रभाव केवल 99 स्कूलों के 4,186 छात्रों (0.18%) पर पड़ता है जो विदेशी भाषाएं पढ़ रहे हैं।

quiz.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding CBSE's submission to the Supreme Court on the three-language policy for Class VI?
options: A) Over 50% of CBSE Class VI students were affected by the exemption order.
B) Digital textbooks for all 22 scheduled Indian languages are made available on the NCERT portal.
C) Less than 10% of CBSE schools currently possess teachers for two distinct native languages.
D) The monitoring committee formed by the Centre is headed by the Chairman of CBSE.
quiz.correct_answer: B) Digital textbooks for all 22 scheduled Indian languages are made available on the NCERT portal.
quiz.explanation: CBSE informed the Supreme Court that Class VI textbooks for all 22 scheduled languages under the Eighth Schedule are published digitally on the NCERT website, while ~93% of surveyed CBSE schools already have qualified teachers for at least two native Indian languages.
